section.paragraph: Divide the entered 24 by 2, then add the three entered allowances of 3, 1, and 3. The arithmetic forms a half-size plus edge allowances. section.paragraph: Display the entered length as whole feet plus the remaining inches. This is a unit-display conversion, not a change to the physical length.

report.paragraph: Bearing-pad dimension along the cap-width dimension chain.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_003_BearingPad_length
section.paragraph: This is dimension C in the embedded Figure 12.5-1. Measure the pad in the direction of the illustrated cap-width calculation. It occupies the part of the chain where the beam bears on the pad.

report.paragraph: Concrete cover between the cap face and the outermost reinforcing steel.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_004_Cap_cover
section.paragraph: This is dimension A in the embedded cap-width figure. It reserves concrete between the exposed cap edge and the reinforcement. The separate B dimension then moves the bearing pad farther inside the reinforcement.

report.paragraph: Extra inset from the outermost cap reinforcement to the bearing-pad edge.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_005_Fig_12_5_1_DimB
section.paragraph: This is dimension B in the embedded Figure 12.5-1. It moves the pad inward beyond the steel location, after the concrete cover has already been counted. It is not additional pad length.

report.paragraph: Distance from the inside bearing-pad edge toward the beam-end detail.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_006_Fig_12_5_1_DimD
section.paragraph: This is dimension D in the embedded Figure 12.5-1. The entered value follows the figure’s no-diaphragm option. This distance is added after the bearing-pad length to reserve the shown space near the beam end.

report.paragraph: Half of the shown no-diaphragm separation used in this end-bent dimension chain.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_007_Fig_12_5_1_DimF
section.paragraph: The displayed expression divides the 3 in separation by 2. It therefore contributes half that separation to this one-sided calculation. In the embedded double-bearing figure, F labels the separation between the opposing end details; the journal uses a half-share here for the stated end-bent adaptation.

report.paragraph: One-sided cap dimension assembled from the entered bearing and edge distances.

section.name: EqNotes_PedBridge_008_Cap_width_min
section.paragraph:
Start with
Cap_cover
, the concrete cover. Add
Fig_12_5_1_DimB
, the inset from the outside reinforcement to the pad, and
BearingPad_length
, the pad length. Then add
Fig_12_5_1_DimD
, the space toward the beam end, and
Fig_12_5_1_DimF
, the entered half-share of the end separation.

The result is the sum of this one-sided chain for the end-bent adaptation noted above. The displayed expression does not double the chain or include the diaphragm-extension dimension E from the embedded double-bearing figure; it should not be read as that figure’s full two-bearing formula.

section.name: PedestalNProvidedNote
section.paragraph: The pier pedestal is modeled as extending the full 4-ft cap width. The two beam ends are separated by the 3-in pier gap, so each beam end is 1.5 in from pier centerline. The provided overlap is therefore one-half the pedestal length minus the beam-end offset.

section.paragraph: Bearing B4 standard service-gravity screening.

Design scope: the Type F gravity screening does not establish combined wind, shear, movement or rotation adequacy. SPI limits include 0.0125-radian static and 0.004-radian cyclic rotation. Check the adopted seat/plate slope and required movement, including creep and shrinkage and applicable lateral actions. The Bridge Movement module remains a thermal-movement calculation, not a complete bearing shear-deflection check.

Seat detailing: the 6-in pedestal and Type F pad place the cap top 8-9/16 in below the adopted beam soffit when no separate plate is present. Cap elevations reference the fixed low-beam soffit. Resolve individual seat grades and any separate plates in the final detail.
